chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), said:

Whichever of the two conditions occurs first, her waiting period (iddah) is completed. If three months pass and she does not see blood in them, her waiting period is completed. And if three menstrual periods pass, her waiting period is completed.
ai.seo_question: How is a divorced woman's waiting period determined if her menstrual cycles are irregular?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the legal mechanism for 'iddah in cases of irregular menstruation (al-qara'at), establishing that the period ends upon the first fulfillment of either three consecutive months without bleeding or three distinct menstrual cycles. It reflects the Shia juristic preference for prioritizing the condition that resolves the uncertainty sooner, ensuring the woman is not bound unnecessarily while maintaining ritual purity standards.
